name: Belief Swap Card
why_it_works: Most people do not avoid a service because of price; they avoid it because of a belief they never examined. Naming that belief out loud makes the viewer feel caught, and replacing it with a calmer, truer one gives them a reason to act without feeling pushed.

hook.pattern: State the limiting belief in the customer's own words, then cross it out on screen.

variables.name: action
variables.description: What the customer keeps putting off, lowercase verb phrase, 3 words or fewer

variables.name: false_condition
variables.description: The condition they think must come first, lowercase verb phrase, 3 words or fewer

variables.name: old_belief
variables.description: The limiting belief as a customer would say it, starting with a capital letter, 6 words or fewer
variables.example: Planning is only for rich people

variables.name: new_belief
variables.description: The truer replacement belief, starting with a capital letter, 7 words or fewer
variables.example: Planning is how people stop guessing

variables.name: first_step
variables.description: A small, low-risk first step, lowercase, 5 words or fewer

visual.prompt: Vertical 4:5 graphic card: the sentence '{{old_belief}}' handwritten in marker on cream paper, a single bold red line striking through it, soft overhead daylight, flat lay

beats.voiceover: You don't need to {{false_condition}} before you {{action}}.

visual.prompt: Vertical 4:5 photo of a calm professional at {{brand}} across a small table from a client, open notebook, warm window light, friendly not salesy, faces softly lit
Vertical 4:5 photo of a phone on a desk showing a calendar booking screen, a coffee cup beside it, morning light, clean tidy desk, {{brand}} logo card in soft focus

slides.headline: The sentence we hear every week
slides.visual_prompt: Cream paper card with '{{old_belief}}' handwritten in marker, flat lay, soft daylight

slides.headline: Catch it in your own words
slides.body: Hear yourself say 'once I...' or 'when I...'? That's the belief talking, not the facts.
slides.visual_prompt: Speech bubble cut from paper reading 'once I...' pinned to a corkboard, soft daylight, vertical 4:5

slides.headline: It's backwards
slides.body: You don't need to {{false_condition}} before you {{action}}.
slides.visual_prompt: Same card, now with a bold red line struck through the sentence

slides.headline: Try this instead
slides.visual_prompt: Clean bold type card in {{brand}} colors with the new belief centered

slides.headline: What the first step looks like
slides.body: It's {{first_step}}. Bring one question, leave with one next step. No homework.
slides.visual_prompt: Calm consultation scene at {{brand}}, two people at a small table, warm light

slides.headline: Save this swap
slides.body: Old: "{{old_belief}}" New: "{{new_belief}}" Read it next time you stall.
slides.visual_prompt: Two index cards side by side, the left crossed out in red, the right circled, flat lay

slides.headline: Your move
slides.visual_prompt: Logo card for {{brand}} with the first step in large type

craft.notes: Quote the old belief exactly as a customer would say it, with no jargon, so the viewer hears their own voice. The strike-through is the visual turn. The new belief must be short enough to remember after one read.

do_not: Mock the viewer for believing the old thing
Make the new belief a promise of results
Use more than one belief per post
compliance: Financial advisors and mortgage brokers: no promises of returns, savings, income or approval; add required firm disclosures and registration details
Dental and chiropractic: no promises of pain-free care or specific outcomes; describe the first visit, not results
Mark any free consultation clearly with its real terms and any limits
Coaches: no income or results promises; any result shown is labelled not typical
